land.text: the Upper Valais, over which 'In 999, King Rudolph III of Burgundy gave all temporal rights and privileges to the Bishop of Sion'

predecessors.note: The Bishop of Sion kept the temporal claim until 1634 ('permanently in 1634'); no dossier exists for the prince-bishopric. The Zenden are drawn as the state from 1416 because the Old Swiss Confederacy page calls the Sieben Zenden 'an independent federation' that allied with Uri, Unterwalden and Lucerne in 1416.

land.text: the Valais, 'incorporated as the canton of Valais of the Helvetic Republic' in 1798, Upper and former Lower Valais together

successors.note: After the Helvetic Republic the Valais was the Rhodanic Republic (1802), the department of Simplon (1810) and a Swiss canton on 4 August 1815; none has a dossier yet.

region.text: the seven Zenden of the Upper Valais

ledger.note: 1416: the Sieben Zenden ally with Uri, Unterwalden and Lucerne. The Old Swiss Confederacy page calls the Sieben Zenden 'an independent federation in the Valais' that 'Became a Zugewandter Ort in 1416 through an alliance with Uri, Unterwalden and Lucerne', followed by a treaty with Bern in 1446; the Canton of Valais page dates the Raron affair rebellion 1414-1420. The page dates the alliance, not a founding; the state's start is the researcher's choice of its first dated act.

region.text: the seven Zenden of the Upper Valais

ledger.note: 1416: the Upper Valais (Sieben Zenden) becomes a Zugewandter Ort (associate) of the Confederacy. Old Swiss Confederacy page: the Sieben Zenden 'Became a Zugewandter Ort in 1416 through an alliance with Uri, Unterwalden and Lucerne', 'followed by a treaty with Bern in 1446'. Mirror of swiss-confederation /ledger/8; an alliance, not subjection, so the nearest rule-4 tint. The pages disagree: the Canton of Valais page says 'On 12 March 1529, Valais became an associate member (Zugewandter Ort) of the Swiss Confederation'; the 1416 of the Swiss table is kept at confidence 2, and the tint could start in 1529 if the colour agent prefers the later page.

region.text: the Lower or Savoyard Valais from the Morge of Conthey down to Martigny

ledger.note: November 1475: the Zenden seize the Savoyard Lower Valais. Canton of Valais page: 'At the outbreak of the Burgundian Wars in 1475, the bishop of Sion and the Zenden made a treaty with Bern. In November of the same year, they seized all Lower or Savoyard Valais up to Martigny'; the Seven Tithings page says 'much of the Lower Valais formerly controlled by the House of Savoy in 1475'. The Morge 'a little below Sion' had been the boundary since 1384 (Canton of Valais page). Repair 2026-11-01: the region was the whole 25 km circle at 46.15N 7.00E, which reached Saint-Maurice and Monthey; the page stops at Martigny, so it is now the three cells (Conthey side, Martigny, Bagnes side) of a 14 km circle at 46.15N 7.20E intersected with the Valais. Saint-Maurice and Monthey follow in March 1476.

region.text: the Lower or Savoyard Valais from the Morge of Conthey down to Martigny

ledger.note: November 1475: the Lower Valais up to Martigny becomes the associate's land. Mirror of swiss-confederation /ledger/15 ('the Valais extends its associate land'), with the corrected region of the gain above: the Swiss event draws the whole 25 km circle, which includes the Saint-Maurice and Monthey cells that the Zenden took only in March 1476; the swiss-confederation owner should narrow /15 and /39 or add a 1476 start.

union.text: Saint-Maurice and the town of Monthey (one 253 km2 cell at this resolution)
the Monthey district's northern part, Vouvry to Le Bouveret (the page names the district of Monthey)
Évian and Thonon, the Chablais east of the Dranse

ledger.note: March 1476: the Zenden take Saint-Maurice, Monthey, Évian and Thonon. Canton of Valais page: 'In March 1476, after the victory of Grandson, they advanced and captured St Maurice, Évian, Thonon and Monthey.' Évian and Thonon are one cell on the south shore of Lake Geneva; Saint-Maurice and the town of Monthey share one cell; the Monthey district is completed with the cell of Vouvry to Le Bouveret (Le Bouveret is named in the 1569 sentence). Repair 2026-11-01: this event was Saint-Maurice alone and the notes said no page dated Monthey or the Chablais; the page does.

region.text: Saint-Maurice and the town of Monthey (one 253 km2 cell at this resolution)

ledger.note: March 1476: Saint-Maurice and Monthey town join the associate's land (the Swiss tint of swiss-confederation /ledger/15 already covers this cell from November 1475, on a wider circle). 'These conquered districts in the Lower Valais were ruled as subject lands by the bishop and the Tithings of the Upper Valais until 1798' (Canton of Valais page).

region.text: the northern part of the Monthey district, Vouvry to Le Bouveret

ledger.note: March 1476: the Monthey district's northern part joins the associate's land, to be lost in 1477 and regained in 1536 with Monthey. The tint covers only the Valais part of the conquest; Évian and Thonon lie outside the canton and carry no Swiss tint. Confidence 2: the page names Monthey, the cell is my reading.

union.text: Monthey, given up in 1477 (its northern cell; the town of Monthey shares the Saint-Maurice cell, which stays drawn at 253 km2 per cell)
Évian and Thonon, the Chablais east of the Dranse

ledger.note: 1477: the Zenden give up Évian, Thonon and Monthey. Canton of Valais page: 'They had to give up the last three districts in 1477 but won them again in 1536.' The page does not name the three; they are read as the last three of the four places of March 1476 (Évian, Thonon, Monthey), Saint-Maurice staying Valais's. Monthey town and Saint-Maurice share one grid cell, so only the Vouvry to Le Bouveret cell and the Évian-Thonon cell leave the drawing. Confidence 2: the year is the page's, the districts are my reading.

region.text: the northern part of the Monthey district, Vouvry to Le Bouveret

ledger.note: 1477: the Monthey district's northern cell leaves the associate's land with the loss above.

union.text: Évian and Thonon, the Chablais east of the Dranse

ledger.note: 1536: the Zenden win Évian, Thonon and Monthey again. Canton of Valais page: 'They had to give up the last three districts in 1477 but won them again in 1536.' Same reading and caveats as the 1477 loss. The neighbouring Thonon, Évian-les-Bains, Chablais and Monthey pages are silent on 1536, so the one page carries it. county-of-savoy has no 1536 loss to the Valais (its 1536 event is Bern's annexation of Vaud).

region.text: the northern part of the Monthey district, Vouvry to Le Bouveret

ledger.note: 1536: the Monthey district's northern cell is the associate's land again, with the regain above.

region.text: Évian and Thonon, the Chablais east of the Dranse

ledger.note: 1569: the Zenden keep Monthey and give back Évian and Thonon. Canton of Valais page: 'In the treaty of Thonon in 1569, Monthey, Val-d'llliez, and Le Bouveret were permanently annexed to Valais.' The page does not say that Évian and Thonon went back to Savoy; that follows from their absence in the list of lands annexed and from their later place in the Duchy of Savoy (Thonon page: the duchy's lands 'reunited after a plebiscite' in 1860). Confidence 2: the year is the page's, the loss is my reading. The county-of-savoy dossier ends in 1559 and hands to house-of-savoy, so the counterpart is house-of-savoy. Monthey, Val-d'Illiez and Le Bouveret are inside the Valais cells and stay drawn.

1634: the prince-bishop gives up secular power for good. 'then permanently in 1634, marking the beginning of the de jure sovereignty of the tithings' (Seven Tithings page); the Canton page: the country became 'the federal Republic of the Seven Tithings'. The bishop had already given up secular power temporarily in 1613. Same state, same colour.

16 March 1798: the Valais becomes a single republic. The Lower Valais districts 'successfully revolted against the Seven Tithings and achieved equal status within the republic' (Canton page); the Seven Tithings page: 'declared as the short lived (16 March to 1 May 1798) République du Valais'. The subject lands stop being subjects; the land is unchanged.

The Canton of Valais page: 'Valais was incorporated into the Helvetic Republic' in 1798; the Swiss Confederacy 'fell to a French invasion in 1798' (Old Swiss Confederacy page); month 3 follows swiss-confederation /ledger/38-39.

region.text: the Valais, incorporated as the canton of Valais of the Helvetic Republic

ledger.note: 1798: the Valais joins the Helvetic Republic. The Seven Tithings page: 'incorporated as the canton of Valais of the Helvetic Republic'; the Canton page: 'incorporated into the Helvetic Republic during the French invasion in 1798, until 1802'. Month 5 is the end of the République du Valais on 1 May 1798; neither page dates the incorporation itself.

1 May 1798: the republic of the Valais ends. The Seven Tithings republic 'was abolished, and merged with its former subject Lower Valais' and the République du Valais ran to 1 May 1798; the Seven Tithings infobox period is 1571-1798.

wars.name: Raron affair
wars.outcome: The Canton of Valais page dates the rebellion 1414 to 1420; Lucerne, Uri and Unterwalden backed the Upper Valais rebels and Bern backed the Rarons. The Seven Tithings page: de facto independence 'since the mid-15th century, as a result of the Raron affair'. No border change on the pages.
wars.note: Repair 2026-11-01: the war is clipped to the state's life, which starts in 1416; the rising began in 1414 ('from 1414 to 1420', Canton of Valais page).

notes: No Cliopatria row: every keyframe is new. Start 1416 follows the swiss-confederation events that already name sieben-zenden; the Seven Tithings page's infobox says 1571-1798 and its text gives de facto sovereignty by the early 17th century and de jure sovereignty in 1634, so the Upper Valais before 1634 was nominally the Bishop of Sion's: a prince-bishopric-of-sion dossier is needed (the Diocese of Sion page gives the countship of about 999, 1630 'relinquished their territorial rule' and 1634 'cede temporal power to the Republic', and no formal start or end), and a gap-filler could move this dossier's start. The 1571-1573 and 1790-1798 infobox sub-periods are unlabelled in the page text read and are not used. Repair 2026-11-01: the November 1475 gain is the Valais between the Morge and Martigny (three cells), the March 1476 capture adds Saint-Maurice, Monthey, Évian and Thonon, the Zenden gave up Évian, Thonon and Monthey in 1477, won them again in 1536 and kept Monthey, Val-d'Illiez and Le Bouveret by the treaty of Thonon of 1569 (Canton of Valais page, the only page that dates these; the Chablais, Monthey, Thonon-les-Bains and Évian-les-Bains pages are silent). At 253 km2 per cell Saint-Maurice and the town of Monthey are one cell, so the 1477 loss draws only the cell of Vouvry to Le Bouveret and the cell of Évian and Thonon. County-of-savoy has no matching loss for 1475, 1476 or 1477, no 1536 regain, and house-of-savoy no 1569 gain. Associate tint: vassal_start/vassal_end events mirror swiss-confederation /ledger/8 (1416), 15 (November 1475), 38 and 39 (1798), with this dossier's narrower regions for the Lower Valais; swiss-confederation /ledger/15 and 39 use the whole 25 km circle (five cells) from November 1475, which includes cells the Zenden took in March 1476, and their owner should narrow them. The Canton of Valais page dates the associate membership 12 March 1529 against 1416 on the Swiss table. swiss-confederation ledger 47 (4 August 1815, 'gain' with counterpart sieben-zenden) names this state after its end: the counterpart should be a Rhodanic Republic / Simplon dossier or the canton itself. The Rhodanic Republic (1802-1810) and the French department of Simplon (1810-1813) have no dossier.
